paper_metadata.title: Quantum Speedup of Monte Carlo Integration with respect to the Number of Dimensions and its Application to Finance

summary: This paper proposes a nested quantum amplitude estimation method for Monte Carlo integration with separable integrands, reducing repeated term-evaluation complexity from N_f,prev ≃ D δ^-1 to N_f,new ≃ δ^-2 when (l δ_rel)^-1 < D. In a credit-portfolio example using PCG, the authors estimate T-counts of about 7.2×10^5 for the previous sequential PRN-based method and 4.6×10^7 for the new method per f-calculation block, with a total T-count ratio of about 0.64 in a representative setting (l = 10^-2, δ_rel = 10^-2, D = 2^20).

experiments.description: Theoretical nested quantum amplitude estimation method for Monte Carlo integration with separable integrands, applied to credit portfolio risk measurement using pseudorandom numbers and PCG; includes comparison against a previous sequential PRN-based quantum Monte Carlo method.

algorithm.variant: nested QAE with pseudorandom-number-based quantum parallelization

hyperparameters.Nsamp: number of samples in outer QAE
hyperparameters.nM: number of qubits in inner QAE control register

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Monte Carlo integrand of separable form F(ε_com,{ε_i};{c_i}) = g(sum_i f(ε_com, ε_i; c_i)); PRNs are generated in superposition using an index register j for samples and i for terms, with qRAM-style loading of c_i and jump-to-index PRN access.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate E[F] where F(ε_com,{ε_i};{c_i}) = g(Σ_{i=1}^D f(ε_com, ε_i; c_i)). For credit risk, L = Σ_i E_i Θ(Z_i, z_i), Z_i = α_i ε_com + sqrt(1-α_i^2) ε_i, and g(L)=Θ(L_α,L) for VaR or g(L)=C L Θ(L_α,L) for CVaR.

problem_instance.description: Credit portfolio risk measurement as a concrete finance use case; loss is computed over obligors with common and individual random variables.

dataset_specification.description: No explicit dataset; model-based credit portfolio with obligor exposures and parameters E_i, α_i, z_i.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity and error analysis; typical-parameter T-count comparison for a representative setting (ndig=16, nPRN=64, nICDF=10^9, nsamp=nobl=20, l=10^-2, delta_rel=10^-2).

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PCG pseudorandom-number generation; inverse-CDF conversion for normal variates via piecewise polynomial approximation; qRAM loading of obligor parameters.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Outer QAE estimation of sample average; comparison of query-count reduction and T-count ratio against previous sequential method.

classical_baselines.method_name: previous sequential prn-based quantum monte carlo method
previous sequential prn-based quantum monte carlo method

speedup_claims.caveats: Refers to oracle-call scaling in error δ: quantum O(δ^-1) vs classical O(δ^-2).

speedup_claims.baseline_method: previous sequential PRN-based quantum Monte Carlo method
speedup_claims.conditions: when the integrand has separable form and D is large enough; benefit if (l δ_rel)^-1 < D
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a reduction in repeated f-calculation queries, not necessarily wall-clock time.

speedup_claims.factor: 64× reduction in per-f T-count ratio relative to previous method
speedup_claims.baseline_method: previous sequential PRN-based quantum Monte Carlo method
speedup_claims.conditions: representative credit-risk setting with ndig=16, nPRN=64, nICDF=10^9, nsamp=nobl=20
speedup_claims.caveats: The new method has higher per-call T-count, but fewer calls; total T-count ratio estimated separately as 0.64 in a typical credit-risk setting.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: previous sequential PRN-based quantum Monte Carlo method
speedup_claims.conditions: typical credit portfolio risk measurement setting with l=10^-2, δ_rel=10^-2, D=2^20
speedup_claims.caveats: Equivalent to about 36% reduction in total T-count; derived from 64(l δ_rel)^-1 / D.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(δ^-1) oracle calls for standard QAE; nested method uses O(δ^-2) inner-QAE calls but reduces repeated term evaluations when D is large, with query reduction factor approximately (l δ_rel)^-1 / D.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(δ^-2) oracle calls for classical Monte Carlo; sequential summation over D terms in the previous method gives N_f,prev ∼ D δ^-1 for the repeated f-calculation block.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: For the repeated f-calculation block, N_f,new ∼ δ^-2; total T-count ratio relative to previous method estimated as 64(l δ_rel)^-1 / D in the representative PCG credit-risk setting.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: N_f,prev ∼ D δ^-1 for the repeated f-calculation block; classical Monte Carlo error scales as O(N^-1/2).
complexity_analysis.crossover_n: Condition for benefit: (l δ_rel)^-1 < D; in the representative setting with l=10^-2, delta_rel=10^-2, D=2^20, the total T-count ratio is about 0.64.

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: (l δ_rel)^-1 < D; representative setting gives (10^-2·10^-2)^-1 / 2^20 ≈ 10^-2 query-reduction ratio, but no hardware crossover is demonstrated
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Large logical circuits for nested QAE, qRAM-style loading, and PCG jump operations; advantage is only in asymptotic query/T-count analysis, not on hardware
limiting_factors: Only theoretical oracle/query and T-count estimates
Nested QAE adds substantial circuit depth
Quadratic-type advantage is not practically established

notes: No physical hardware experiment is performed; hardware.type is not specified because the paper is a theoretical resource-estimation study.

num_qubits is not given as a single total register size for the full algorithm; only register roles and sizes such as nM, nsamp, nobl are described, so total qubit count is inferred as not directly reported.
Circuit depth is not given explicitly; only asymptotic query/T-count estimates are provided.
The paper reports only theoretical complexity reductions and a representative T-count comparison, not a hardware demonstration.
Classical Monte Carlo is used as a scaling baseline; no empirical quantum-vs-classical benchmark is performed.
